name: Oregon Health & Science University

profile.address: 505, Northwest 185th Avenue, Amberglen, Beaverton, Washington County, Oregon, 97006
profile.reading:
This facility in Washington County, Oregon is attributed to Oregon Health and Science University (OHSU), the state's academic health center and largest hospital based research and teaching institution, headquartered on Marquam Hill in Portland. The building sits in the Amberglen area of Beaverton, along Northwest 185th Avenue, inside a technology and office corridor that also hosts networking, semiconductor and corporate campuses associated with the broader Silicon Forest cluster west of Portland.

OHSU is not a commercial data center operator. Like most large academic medical centers, it runs its own enterprise IT infrastructure to support electronic health records, clinical imaging, research computing and administrative systems across its hospital, clinic and university campuses. Locating that infrastructure away from the main Marquam Hill hospital complex is a common resiliency practice among health systems, since a facility physically separated from the primary campus reduces the chance that a single incident, such as a fire, flood or power outage, disrupts both patient care operations and the systems that support them.

OHSU previously operated a satellite campus in Washington County through the former Oregon Graduate Institute (OGI), which it absorbed in 2001 and largely vacated by 2014 when those programs relocated to Marquam Hill. Public sources describe that transition in general terms but do not establish whether this particular Washington County data center descends from the OGI era footprint or is a separate facility built or leased specifically for enterprise IT use. Either origin would be consistent with a university and hospital system owned facility rather than a colocation or cloud provider site, and neither points to a commercial tenant.

Because OHSU treats this building as internal infrastructure supporting protected health information and research systems, it does not publish power capacity, square footage, tier rating or tenancy details for it, and no county permit or property record specific to this address has surfaced in the sourcing behind this entry. That silence is itself informative: hospital systems generally decline to publicize the location or specifications of data centers holding clinical and research data, for security and regulatory reasons, not because nothing is there. The entry will be updated if verifiable capacity, ownership or facility detail becomes publicly available.

reading:
Oregon Health and Science University is the state's only public academic health centre, running hospitals, clinics and research institutes across Oregon and southwest Washington from its Marquam Hill campus in Portland. It appears in a data centre registry for the ordinary reason that a large hospital system and research university is also a large IT operation, carrying electronic health records, imaging archives, genomics pipelines and cluster computing for thousands of researchers, and it chose to build for that rather than lease.

The single row this registry holds for OHSU is its West Campus facility in Washington County, off Northwest 185th Avenue, the campus better known as the home of the Oregon National Primate Research Center and the Vaccine and Gene Therapy Institute. The building is unusual enough to be worth describing. It is an aluminium geodesic dome, opened in July 2014 at a reported cost of 22 million dollars, covering about 8,000 square feet. It was designed in house by Perry Gliessman, then director of technology services in OHSU's Information Technology Group, rather than by a data centre developer.

The cooling is the point of the design. Air enters through large intakes at the base and leaves through vents at the top by natural convection, with a vegetative bioswale around the building assisting. Chillers, computer room air conditioners, dehumidifiers and exhaust fans were all designed out, leaving air handling units as the only mechanical plant. Reporting at the time placed the dome about 34 percent better than the average self reporting United States data centre for 2014.

The power figures deserve care, because published accounts give two numbers that are easily confused. The facility is described as 4 megawatts of total electrical capacity, of which roughly 0.2 megawatts serves non IT equipment, leaving about 3.8 megawatts available to IT load, with individual racks supported up to 25 kilowatts. That 3.8 megawatt figure is a genuine critical IT capacity, which is rarer in this registry than it should be, and it is not a utility service rating, a standby generator rating or an on site generation figure. No separate diesel or utility number has been published for the site.

Two limits on what this row represents. The dome shares load with OHSU's primary facility in downtown Portland, which this registry does not hold, so one row understates the university's footprint. And OHSU later licensed the dome design to a startup called Server Dome, whose marketing claims of roughly 30 percent lower construction cost, 80 percent lower maintenance cost and a fifteen to twenty year service life are vendor claims about a product, not verified measurements of this building.
